ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A$, $O$, $B$ lie on the same line, and $OC$ bisects $\angle AOB$. If $\angle COD = 28^\circ$, and $OE$ bisects $\angle BOD$, find the degree measure of $\angle COE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OE$ bisects $\angle BOD$,\\
we have $\angle DOE = \frac{1}{2}\angle BOD = 31^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle COE = \angle DOE + \angle COD = 31^\circ + 28^\circ = \boxed{59^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $OE$ bisects $\angle BOD$,\\ we have $\angle DOE = \frac{1}{2}\angle BOD = 31^\circ$,\\ hence, $\angle COE = \angle DOE + \angle COD = 31^\circ + 28^\circ = \boxed{59^\circ}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, O, B are on the same horizontal straight line, with O in the middle; ray OC extends vertically upward from O; rays OD and OE extend from O toward the upper right, and OD is between OC and OE, while OE is between OD and OB. Reasoning: Because A, O, B are collinear, ∠AOB is a straight angle of 180°; OC bisects ∠AOB, therefore ∠COB=90°. It is known that ∠COD=28°, and OD is inside ∠COB, so ∠BOD=90°-28°=62°. OE bisects ∠BOD, so ∠DOE=62°÷2=31°. Since going from OC to OE must pass through OD, ∠COE=∠COD+∠DOE=28°+31°=59°.
